utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.text: Major, can you begin please by giving us your full name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, did you testify about certain matters related to Sarajevo and the Dragomir Milosevic case?

utterances.text: I wonder, Your Honours, if we could please have Exhibit 65 ter 09386 on the screen. And Your Honours, I should have signalled Major Overgard is a 92 ter witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Major, you'll see there at the top of the page that the testimony is dated the 18th of January, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I wonder if we could turn over the next page, please, Madam Registrar. And scroll down and the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, major, do you recognise that as a transcript of your testimony given in the Dragomir Milosevic case on the 18th of January 2007?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review that transcript of testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I did yesterday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And is it true and correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions this morning, would you answer in the same way?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If that could please be tendered as a Prosecution exhibit.

The pages themselves have been notified in the 92 notice which has been filed with the Chamber. The non-relevant parts have been redacted so that all that remains is the relevant testimony of Major Overgard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. That exhibit is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P479.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Major, did you also testify on the following day, the 19th of January?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we please have, Your Honours, Exhibit 65 ter 09387 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Major, again we can see the date of Friday the 19th of January on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And do you see there the commencement of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Again, Major, did you have the opportunity to review this transcript of your testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: It is tendered, and it is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the two transcripts, Major, did you also earlier provide a statement to OTP, Office of the Prosecutor investigators in April 1996?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Major, do you recognise -- wait for the -- Major, do you recognise that as the statement that you provided to OTP officials in 1996?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Again, did you review the contents of that statement yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is it true and correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD

utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If that statement, which a redacted statement could also be tendered as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. What 65 ter number did you give it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It is 09388, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 09388. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P481.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Finally, Major, in preparation for your testimony in the D. Milosevic case, did you provide some limited further information to OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could please have, Your Honours, 65 ter number 09389 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Major, do you recognise that as a record of the remarks that you made prior to your testimony in the D. Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Again, did you have the opportunity to review that document yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are the contents true and correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They would be the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Major. Your Honours, could we please tender that as an exhibit also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P482.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be permitted, I have a short summary of the testimony and remarks contained in that statement which I'd like to read into the record at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Major Overgard was posted to Sarajevo as a United Nations Military Observer, UNMO, during the period from late October 1994 to 1 May, 1995. After an initial posting for around ten days and an area held by VRS forces, he was posted to Hrasnica within territory held by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He remained there until 1 May, 1995. During his time in Hrasnica, Major Overgard and his team investigated many shelling and sniping incidents. During his time there, there were casualties almost every day, most of them civilian. The greatest casualties occurred during November and December, 1994, and April 1995. Of all the shelling and sniping investigations undertaken by Major Overgard and his team during the six month period in Hrasnica, identified VRS-held territory as the source of fire. Most of the shelling incidents investigated by Major Overgard involved civilian victims. All the incidents of sniping investigated by Major Overgard involved civilian victims. The VRS had mortar positions between Ilidza and Blazuj and in the area of the Lukavica barracks. It was mainly from these two directions that Hrasnica, including the areas of Butmir and Sokolovic were shelled. The centre of Hrasnica was a residential civilian area with no military installations. Sniping from Butmir to came from Ilidza and the Famos factory. There was regular shelling and sniping of civilians using the road by forces of the VRS and Ilidza. There was also a lot of sniping of civilians using a bridge at Butmir by those VRS forces. Major Overgard estimates that during his time in Hrasnica, 30 to 40 civilians were killed as a result of the sniping and shelling incidents he investigated alone. Thank you, Your Honours, and finally there are some matters raised in the 92 ter materials that have been provided which I'd like to ask some questions on to clarify. They fall into two categories. Firstly a number of occasions which I'd like Major Overgard to demonstrate for us on a map; and secondly to clarify some comments he has made about air-bombs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I wonder, Your Honours, if we could please have Exhibit P439 up on the screen. And it is map number 8 in the court binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Major, in your testimony and in your statements, you mention a number of different locations in Sarajevo, locations where you were posted, locations where civilians were targeted by VRS forces, and the location of VRS forces. And what I'd like to do with you is to just identify some of those locations you speak of in your previous testimony, and in your statements, and identify those on this map. What you see here is a map of Sarajevo. What we can do with the technology that we have is to enlarge this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And Your Honours, if we could just, thank you, enlarge the -- if we could scroll down just a fraction and scroll to the left just a fraction. A little more.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: First of all, Major, do you recognise what is shown on the map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it's from the airport and south Hrasnica area in the foot of Igman mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. First of all the airport that you just mentioned which is referred to in your statement, is that -- I wonder if Mr. Usher -- Madam Usher, if we could provide the Major with the electronic pen. If you could just draw a line along the runway of the airport, please?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, and maybe mark that with the letter A.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you make that A a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, first of all, you mentioned that your -- when you first arrived in Sarajevo, Major, you were posted in VRS territory at a location known to UNMOs as Sierra Whiskey 1?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you mark on that map where Sierra Whiskey 1 was?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: If I'm correct I believe it was in this area they had a team location.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you mark that please with SW1.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. You say in your testimony that you were there for a period of ten days or so before you were moved to a second location, Sierra Sierra 2?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you mark, please, for us where Sierra Sierra 2 was?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: River comes down, okay, so here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the settlement in which we see Sierra Sierra 2, is that Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Hrasnica was territory held by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the area you've marked as Sierra Whiskey 1 was territory held by the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we first produce that marked map as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P440 [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Sorry the exhibit number? 440.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is 440 or 483.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's 483, I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we please go back to a blank version of the map which is P439, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Major, you then mention a number of areas where civilians were targeted or at least shelled and sniped by VRS forces. The first of those that I'd like to talk about is the Igman Road. Can you draw a line for us please, along the Igman Road?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The road comes here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is there an area along that road that was more susceptible to shelling and sniping than any other part of the road?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Well, the lower part here, you can see from this big turn up here and down longwards, there were direct missile contacts to the Ilidza area there was heavy shelling, sniping, and shooting to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Would you please mark that line with IR.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And is this the road that you also refer to in your testimony or statements as "the blue road" or the "convoy road"?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You also describe in addition to Hrasnica being shelled and sniped, an area called Butmir?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you see that on the map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. Has to be, it's a bit here, so it has to be this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you mark that with a B, please.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You talk about the bridge and civilians being shot on the bridge as they entered Sarajevo. Can you see the bridge on the map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I believe the bridge is the one marked here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You also mention an area that was targeted called Sokolovic?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you see that on the map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I think it's more to the right. I'm not sure anymore about the precise location of Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: When you say to the right, to the right of where?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The right on the map. The right on the side of the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: To the right of the airport at some point?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Could you circle Hrasnica for us?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And maybe put an H next to that.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And Your Honours, could we please tender that as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is Exhibit P484.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Madam Registrar. And to a blank version of the map one more time, please. P439.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: This time, Major, I want to talk about the VRS positions that you referred to in your testimony and in your statements. Firstly, you describe the source of a lot of the shelling and sniping as being Ilidza. Can you mark Ilidza for us on that map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. You also describe an area called Blazuj.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do we see that on the map as well?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We can say Blazuj is this area here, where the team location was for Sierra Whiskey 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. You also describe some sniping as coming from the Famos factory, or the area of the Famos factory?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it was this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is the Famos factory actually that collection of dark buildings?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It is?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You mention also firing from the Lukavica barracks?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do we see those on the map, or do we need to move the map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They are somewhere in this area. I do not remember the exact position.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you -- we'll need to mark those so that we can refer to those later. Could you please put an LB next to that line that you've just drawn?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you please put an F next to the marking around the Famos factory?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you please put an I around the marking you've drawn to Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And a B please around Blazuj. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, can we please tender that map as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that will be Exhibit P485.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Finally, Major, during your testimony in Dragomir Milosevic, you spoke of modified air-bombs. Air-bombs with rocket motors attached to them that were used by the VRS. Firstly, can you tell us which forces or from where, which VRS forces used those air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I experienced one of these bombs during my time in Hrasnica, and it came from Ilidza and into a town 300 metres from our accommodation in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Major, those are all the question that I have for you at this stage. My learned friend for the Defence may have some questions for you if you kindly wait there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Thomas. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Overgard. My name is Novak Lukic, and I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Perisic; and on behalf of his Defence now, I will put some questions to you. First of all, I'd like to ask you about your service and what kind of jobs you did while you were in Sarajevo. If I understood correctly, you were part of the UNMO team in Sarajevo in charge of investigating and establishing the sites where missiles fell including infantry weapons and air-bombs, modified air-bombs; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I can say also mortars, mortar fire, artillery. Missiles are, you can say, kind of guided missile, and all the rest are bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Earlier you attended a three week course in Finland for these -- to prepare for these activities; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the course among others, you learned about the analysis of the matters or issues that you were later to carry out or conduct, and this included the effects or consequences or impacts of these projectiles; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before this course during your military service, you had never been involved in criminal investigations, as it were, if I may put it in general terms?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in the former Yugoslavia, you spent a few days in Zagreb to begin with, where you also attended a course about -- for about six days, but this course did not relate to this particular area of investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what type of instruments did you have at your disposal when you would arrive at a site to investigate an incident?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Mostly we always had the compass to give the exact direction where we believe the mortar or the artillery piece came from. It is a summary of what you find when what angle hits the ground with, which side of the crater the splints have gone into the ground, and you can find out from where it fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a layperson, I'd like to ask you this, is there any particular instrument that can be used to establish the angle from which a projectile or a shell is arriving?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not as I know that there are anything to give exact position, but you can give a direction and from the angle also if you are very good at it, find what distance approximately it's fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us on the basis of what you established the distance from which the shell was fired?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, I can't give the exact distance. I only in my reports pointed at directions, and I never had the education to find correct distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there anyone on your team who was an expert on determining exactly the distance and not just the direction?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when you decided on the direction that you supposed that that was where the projectile had come from, this was just in general terms. You could never establish with any kind of precision where it exactly came from; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct. If you are not hearing outgoing bang, from that when it lands, you can say from where, but that was very seldom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For my better understanding, could you just explain to us what was more seldom, was it more seldom that you could see where a projectile had been fired from; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Very seldom that we heard the outgoing, you could say bang then and then could also identify a landing, an explosion from an artillery piece or a mortar piece. But it happened when we was close to the confrontation line against Ilidza, and we could hear from the hill-side behind the barracks in Ilidza; and we could hear come from there, and then it landed somewhere inside our AOR. And AOR is area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were frequently on site for these investigations together with members of the local authorities, primarily the police, and I mean the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We had also -- we worked together also with them but we did our investigation, they did theirs, there were no cooperation but they were given our conclusions and we always two UNMOs doing the investigation together so there should be -- should not be any misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was not whether you worked together, but whether you were on site at the same time, whether you could observe how they did their job, whether they were there at the same time? Just that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the members of those teams who conducted investigations have some instruments that you did not have in their investigations?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they ever complain to you about your lack of expertise, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You wanted to offer them some expert assistance because you felt that they were not as well trained as you were; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, we did not offer them assistance. We gave them the results of our investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you thought that among them, there were also people who were policemen, not necessarily professional, not necessarily professional policemen, but people who had just been put through a course for policemen?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We found that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, Mr. Overgard, that the most reliable method in conducting an investigation properly, regardless of what the cause of the accident is, is to leave everything as it is until the sight can be thoroughly reviewed and observed?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, can't do too much damage to a crater from an artillery piece or a mortar. You are just doing the observations. We might also find the tail of the artillery piece in the crater, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is crater analysis the only way that you can determine where a projectile had come from, the direction?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, when it comes to artillery mortar firing, that's the only thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it relevant in determining the direction whether a projectile had hit a hard surface or the ground or a wall or some other object?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If it hits a wall, you can only see the hole, and we will not have anything to investigate from to determine where it come from. It has to hit the ground whether it is hard ground or soft ground, it's real not as long as the detonation has been there when it hits, we will find a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if I understood correctly, the direction can only be determined if the crater is in the ground regardless of what type of surface it is?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, that is for sure. If it hits a roof, for instance, it might not detonate; and from the angle when it stops in the roof or it goes into some furniture inside, you can also find the direction without -- not on the ground, but that is when it's detonation has been there, it is hard to find if you are not on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also took advantage of eye-witnesses who would provide you information about where they think the projectile had come from?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, we took statements from witnesses. Sometimes it was, I can't give you numbers, but there's been a few occasions we had witnesses telling us from where it was fired. Especially is that when it comes to sniping we had to rely on witnesses because we had to know what direction the victim faced when it was hit, then to find out on the body from where the shot has been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, speaking of the sniping incidents that you investigated, whether you -- when you arrived on site whether there were dead bodies there or whether you only could look at the dead bodies in the morgue?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We had both -- incidents of both. We have sometimes we came early enough to see the bodies before they were transported to the morgue, but we never inspected them before they came to the morgue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose that witness statements were interpreted to you by the local interpreters who were in your team; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, we had local interpreters in teams that always followed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were on the Sarajevo battle-field, did you ever -- were you actually ever on site at the moment when the incident occurred, you personally?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, not as I remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, when you arrived on site, the witnesses would introduce themselves and then you would take statements from them; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. If we -- we asked around if anybody saw what happened, and we got witnesses in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up the same map on the screen. I believe it's P439, the blank exhibit. Could we have that on the screen. And especially could we have the Hrasnica area blown up. A bit more, please. Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the building where your base was in Hrasnica, if you could just give us a general idea or would you like this to be blown up a bit more?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I think I'll manage. Let me see. We were somewhere around here. Just in the [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please put a number 1 next to this mark?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We also know that the command post of the 4th Motorised Brigade of the BH Army was in Hrasnica as well. Could you please show us if you can where that location was?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They had a location, a HQ in a big building, I believe it is this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that with a 2. Number 2.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also know that there was another command post there of a BH Army unit of a lower level, which was also in Hrasnica; correct? Would you please mark that spot as well?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There was a company in the area of the confrontation line have to be in somewhere here in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark that with a 3.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was -- that the command post of the 155th Motorised Brigade of the BH Army was in Butmir, which was not too far from your location?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I know that they said that they should be there, but I never was there myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The locations that you marked, are those institutions, as it were, the HQs, they were on civilian premises; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you had meetings with a commander of the 4th Motorised Brigade, did you know or do you know now how many men that brigade numbered?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that it numbered anywhere between 3.000 to 3.500 men, would that help jar your memory?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, it will not because I never saw so many soldiers in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would please like this map to be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your work did you have any contacts with the corps HQ in Sarajevo, with some man from the command of that corps?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago, at the request of my learned colleague Mr. Thomas, you marked the road leading to Mount Igman. Do you know whether that road was protected by BH Army units?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: There were some positions and -- in that area, but you see where I marked the area 3, that was the area where they had some positions and there was some fire extension against Ilidza area. That was the only position. The road up to Igman, I drove it a lot of times myself, and never had -- there were no positions protecting the road. It's late in 1995, the French brigade had a position in the lower part of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Mount Igman was under the control of the BH Army during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And would you also agree that the Igman Road was a line that connected Sarajevo to the other parts of the territory that were under the control of BH?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It might be so, yes, they got their delivery of food and so on coming down that road. It came to Hrasnica and somehow they managed to get it into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Everything that came from Igman went via Hrasnica, right, towards the parts of Sarajevo that were under the control of the BH Army; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I have to believe that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also know that all military assistance and aid, military equipment, personnel arrived only along that road to Sarajevo to meet the needs of the BH Army; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I think if they had equipment, people, they were walking down the mountain all over, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then again went via Hrasnica; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please still have this map here. Another copy, because I'd like to ask the witness to mark something else, if he remembers, while the map is still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point you saw a tunnel being dug by the Butmir airport. You saw that with your very own eyes. Could that be marked on this map, the place where you saw the tunnel being dug?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah. I just can give a general area and had to be somewhere here. I don't know the exact position anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please place number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you saw that something was being dug there at that locality, the local authorities told you that they were digging something there for water supply purposes; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, there was some explanation; it could not be correct, so we just waited when inspector regularly to see what was being done there. But we were not, never allowed to stop in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They did not let you stop in that area?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I say "they" --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: So the -- there was people in civilian clothes mostly doing the work there, but they didn't want us to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I say "they," I mean the authorities of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Later on you heard that a tunnel had been dug underneath the airport and that that was the route that was used for bringing people and equipment to the area that was under the control of the BH Army; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we still have map there, so that we don't have to go back to that again, do you see Kovaci on the map? Could you please mark that with a number 2, or would you like us to zoom in on it?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: A bit more in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's going to delete.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, if this map will be admitted into evidence, then I will ask for it to be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then that map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this marked map will be Exhibit D35, and I would like to state for a record that I stated a different number for the previous document, that should be D35 exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you are saying, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Exhibit number assigned to the previous document tendered by Mr. Lukic was given a number D33, where instead, it should have been given a number Exhibit D34. And the current map will then be Exhibit D35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to have the same map, but could it please be enlarged a bit, rather the Hrasnica area. The left hand part of the map, that's what I'd like to deal with now. Could it go up a bit -- no, it's fine, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like us to mark two more locations Kovaci or rather the place where you saw the BH Army mortars, I'd like to ask you something about that, so could you show us where that was, where the four mortars were?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Well, there were some houses close, it has to be in this area here. Doesn't look ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that this will do.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: In this area here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please put an M there.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that the area called Kovaci?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the M stands for?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to put a question to the witness. I thought well, we were dealing with another topic but now I'd like to put this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point when you toured the area, you saw four mortars of the BH Army at this location; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. They were after we had confronted the brigade with it, they were removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we are dealing with this map, let me ask you about another incident too. The place where you saw a 17-year-old girl being hit by sniper fire in Sokolovic, can that be shown on this map or do we need another map?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I think I can see that, that was somewhere along this road here, in this particular -- in this area, I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please put the letter S there.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you about that incident specifically. You saw this girl walking down the road. You were in your vehicle and you went on; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then after about an hour, an inspector of the BH Army police asked you to come to the morgue, and that's where you recognised the girl that you had seen previously on the road. You actually recognised her body; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not see the actual moment when she was hit, it was subsequently that you saw her corpse at the morgue?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She was hit -- or rather, that was concluded on the basis of the postmortem that was done afterwards. The exit/entry wound was so big that a conclusion drawn was that a 12.7-millimetre bullet had been used, which was rather unusual for a sniper, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was. But there was some heavy firing into that area that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The fire that you heard that day at that location, did it come from both sides, if I can put it that way? Did you hear it from different locations? Or was it that you had just heard that there had been firing? Did you personally hear any gun-fire?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, that day I heard the firing. I heard that it was a heavier weapon than a normal machine-gun, so it had to be something like 12.7, 14.6, whatever; and the fire came from east of the airport area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time when you were touring the locations at Igman, you saw these same weapons being used by the BH Army; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I saw one 12.7 sniper gun late that winter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more question in relation to this incident. As for the location from which the bullet came, the one that hit the girl, you established that on the basis of the wounds in her body and also the direction of movement that you saw before that; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At any rate, you don't know whether in the meantime she turned around and started walking the other way, you have no way of concluding what the situation actually was; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Correct. You just had to assume that she was still walking somewhere and had -- she will not be out there walking for no reasons because there was firing in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to put a few questions to you in relation to the shelling. From whom did you receive information in terms of you having to go to a particular location to carry out an onsite investigation related to shelling?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Well, we could get information from the civilian police, or if we heard a detonation, we went on site on our own in initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I read in your statement that for the most part you went out with an investigating judge. Was that a regular thing? Would an investigating judge always be there when you would come, or would you go together, or what happened?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, with some occasions, she was with us. It was especially the days after the bomb that exploded, and then she was present in the area; so she followed everything we investigated on that side for that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A general question in relation to the incidents that you dealt with. Generally speaking, from the moment when you would find out that an incident had occurred, how many time would elapse until you would actually arrive at the actual site? Can you give us any idea about the time involved?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It all depended on if it still was shelling going on or it was just a single detonation. If there was a single detonation, you could be there within ten minutes. If there was shelling going on, we had to wait until that had stopped. And then there was a lot of incidents or detonation we never saw because we couldn't go to the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more question, and then I think I will have completed this particular line of questioning. While you were working on onsite investigation, there were never any representatives of the Bosnian Serb authorities in any sense, the Army of Republika Srpska, an investigating judge, the police, no one; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not in Hrasnica area, no. As long as I was in the team in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we can take the break now, Your Honours. And I would like to tender this document into evidence, the map that hasn't been admitted yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And on that note, can we take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Overgard, when you wanted to tour the frontline, if I can put it that way, you had to address the military authorities and they had to make it possible for you to go to these more dangerous zones; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They wanted us to do that, yes. Although, investigations done close to the front line we also did that on our own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There were also cases when you were told that you shouldn't go, and then you didn't go to visit certain zones; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you toured the frontline, that's what I'm going to call it, but let me put it this way, did you go close to the line of separation or the frontline of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, a couple of times I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Sarajevo and in Hrasnica, did you notice that the line moved in any way --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- to anyone's advantage?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that it was stable, the line of separation; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to put a few more questions to you, with regard to something completely different. You said that once you had an onsite investigation in relation to an air-bomb. I'm not going to ask you about the incident itself, but I'm going to ask but the procedure involved. I would be interested in hearing about your relationship with the Bosnian authorities on that occasion. So you can just give me yes or no answers whether I understood the information provided by you correctly with regard to that incident. On that day you heard a loud explosion in the morning when you were still at your base; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then you tried to contact the local police and you even went to the police station; however, you didn't find anyone there?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Immediately afterwards, you went to the scene, and among the debris, you noticed legs and feet belonging to a man who was wearing camouflage uniform and boots; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when you discovered that on the spot, then the commander of the 4th Motorised Brigade showed up; and he asked you to go back to your base, and he removed you from the scene; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you would return to the base, and you stayed there until the late afternoon in the building at your base; and the BH Army put three soldiers at the entrance into the building, and they did not let you leave the building; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, two members of the French battalion came to see what was going on, and they were not allowed to leave your base either; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, may I just interrupt you and find out something. I notice that you are asking questions on the redacted part of the tendered statement. You are doing that deliberately and purposefully. Are you opening the redaction and saying that we can also have sight of up redacted version because we have a copy of it, but I notice that what was tendered by the Prosecution, this part is redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. All of these questions pertain to his testimony and, indeed, his witness statement, the part that is redacted too. I uploaded the unredacted part too in e-court. So if the witness challenges something then I'm going to show you a certain page -- show him, rather, the page of the transcript involved. I just wanted to go through this entire procedure with him without going into the entire testimony with regard to this incident because it's rather lengthy. However, it's a public transcript. His entire testimony is. I can give you page references in respect of the questions that I'm putting to the witness so that you would have that for your own information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't have any quarrel with you doing what you are doing, all I -- I'm -- the reason I'm asking the question is whether the unredacted version of the statement should now be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I don't want it to be tendered. I just want to get to some facts that I'd like to get through his answers. I don't want the statement or parts of the transcript in the evidence. However, if there are some contradictions, in terms of the answers he is giving me now, then I'm going to show him parts of his previous testimony. That's the way we handled it before too. If there's anything contradictory then I'm going to put a particular transcript page to him or a page of a statement and ask him about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I'll go back to the chronology. Sometime in the late afternoon you were allowed to go back to the scene because your liaison officer had contacted the BH authorities, and late in the afternoon around 1900 hours you came to the scene once again; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact timings, but late in the evening, yes, or afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, at the scene you no longer found any trace of the legs and feet with camouflage uniform and boots that you had observed beforehand; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you went to the site itself on those two occasions on that day, that is to say, after the police station first, and then later on in the late afternoon, on the scene you did not find any fragments that could have been helpful to you in terms of reconstructing what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We found some fragments but we did not know what this was. I believe it was that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the next morning again the Bosnian authorities did not allow you to go to the scene, you stayed on base until around noon; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then when you came to the scene, the investigation authorities of the BH side showed you certain fragments and pieces of clothing and so on that were used to reconstruct the incident; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that with the inspector, you went to the morgue where you were shown the corpse of a woman and you were told that she was a casualty in that incident; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another question that I did not find anywhere in the transcript. As for the inspector that took you to the morgue or any other representatives of the BH authorities that you contacted during those days, did you tell them about having seen the traces of the feet in boots that you observed on that day? Did you tell them that you had observed that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I believe so because I got the explanation that this was a soldier and he was not badly hurt, so he was alive. It would only be one casualty in that bomb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you say he was not badly hurt, or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Or was he badly hurt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not badly hurt. He was nearly unharmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did that story sound convincing to you since you had seen the area yourself?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I should not speculate in that because he was not there anymore, and I was not able to find out anything more about it. Of course, he could be alive and sound, but I have no evidence one way or the other so we just left that story.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you now to explain what it was that you saw, the image that you saw. In the debris, you saw these legs and feet of a man in camouflage uniform wearing boots, that's what you saw on the first day; right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the legs coming out of a lot of stones from the house and this wall that fell down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when you saw this, the brigade commander asked that you be removed from the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: He came -- as I discovered this, he came at the same moment and he wanted us to go back to our accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To be completely clear, let me ask you, so when you subsequently discussed this with the local authorities they told you that there had been a BH Army soldier there who had been slightly injured; correct?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, there was a person. They did not mention a soldier especially. But just I saw only was the legs and the camouflage trousers and boots, military boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because on page 35, you mention the word "soldier," that the soldier had not been seriously wounded. You said that a few moments ago, that it was a soldier who hadn't been seriously wounded?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, you can assume that it was a soldier since he had a uniform and boots, but they referred to it as a person, not badly injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just another question in relation to this incident and what you yourself saw, and what you were unable to see later on. Were you able to compile a report to your superiors that you had gone to the scene and that you weren't able to remain there because you had a sort of clash with local authorities. Is that something that you mentioned in your report to your superior?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I believe it was mentioned because we were detained in our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you Mr. Overgard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Any re-examination, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit D34 on the screen, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, Major, you recognise this map as one that you marked during the course of your testimony this morning. The number 2, the circle with the number 2, just to refresh your memory, was where you marked the headquarters of the 4th Motorised Brigade of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You want to ask you about those headquarters and the location of those headquarters, and the shelling activity that Hrasnica was subjected to. During your time there, was the premises of the -- or the buildings occupied by the 4th Motorised Brigade the subject of shelling by VRS forces?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: We never had any investigations in their buildings, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was there anything like a pattern of shelling focused around that building?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The shelling was all over Hrasnica. We had investigations all along in all the areas. Not anything specific where there were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you had -- if those military headquarters were the target, would you have expected a different pattern of shelling?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I would believe that the shelling will be closer to the specific buildings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was the headquarters of the 4th Motorised Brigade actually in the centre of what we would describe the centre of the settlement, the focus of the town?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah, it was in a big block with the -- in a basement, it was a big house for civilians, it was in the basement on that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of the headquarters was there a -- any civilian concentration?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes, it was civilians all around in that area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And in the other areas of Hrasnica where the shells landed, were there any other such military installations?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were asked a series of questions about a 17-year-old girl who was shot by snipers, and this was not a part of the information you gave in your statement or testimony which is before this Tribunal as part of your 92 ter package, your evidential package that we already put in. But because you were asked about that, I just want to just go over that a little briefly with you. First of all, can you explain a little -- can you tell Your Honours about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes. I believe we had been into the headquarters in the centre of Sarajevo, me and one other UNMO, and on our way passing the place where they were digging tunnel, we saw this girl, she was walking against the houses. This was along where, you could say along this road where there was no houses, just where we saw her; but then closer to the houses on the end of the road when we came there, there was a lot of shooting, and it was heavy shooting this time. It was not only light machine-gun, it was heavy machine-gun. When we came to accommodation, the local police after awhile they contacted us, and I had, because the other guys were occupied with maintenance and generator and car, I went with the policeman alone to the morgue for that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, the shooting you describe as going on at the time, was -- was this shooting at the confrontation lines? What sort of shooting was it?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: It was shooting. And when we protested to our liaison officer in the HQ, we got the answer that they were shooting to get the people away from the area where they were digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Digging the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: This was from the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You spoke of the bullet that killed this girl. Firstly, was she civilian or military?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: She was civilian definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Would that have been apparent to anyone who cared to look?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You said that she was killed using a 12.7-millimetre round, and my learned friend asked you whether you had ever seen such a weapon in the hands of the army of the ABiH, but what I want to ask you is whether the VRS forces had such weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Not as I had seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I did never see that, as I remember. But for sure when they also had heavier weapons because we found fragments on the convoy road from 30 millimetres and 20 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say that this girl was shot by the Bosnian/Serb army, where had the shots come from?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The shots came from the hill-side west of the air field.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: West of the air field?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. I wonder --

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Sorry, Lukavica barracks are around there, as I remember. Okay. Show that again. Of course, east of the air field.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Maybe we can have Exhibit D35 on the screen, which is the map that deals with this incident, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, I think this is the map that deals with that incidents. Do you recall what you marked on the map as being the site of where this girl was killed?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you mark on the map there where you found the source of fire to be?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Has to be somewhere in here, this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And who held that territory?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: That was Serbian territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could just mark -- VRS forces?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you could just put "VRS" there, please.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If that could please be produced as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: D35 as marked is admitted as an exhibit. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P486.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If I could just have a brief moment with one of my learned colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about the occasion where you saw a 12.7-millimetre weapon in the position of the army -- in the position of the ABiH. Where did you see that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I believe it was on Mount Igman. We had just passed a group of soldiers up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And were all of those soldiers armed with that weapon?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, that was only one weapon with that one. That was a brand new roaming 12.7 sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: From there position, did they have a line of sight into the area where this girl was killed or any part of ABiH-held Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: They had to be very far up in the hill-side on Mount Igman then, but from that position they did not have -- where I saw the weapon there was not any line of sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are you able to mark on the map that's still on the screen the sort of area where you saw this weapon?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I'm not sure where it was anymore. I have to ... but I was on the road, convoy road somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Which we see in the bottom left-hand corner of the map; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, we've spoken about the tunnel, and you've spoken about the tunnel. Was the tunnel of strategic significance to the people of ABiH-held Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: For sure it would be because it would do it a lot more easy to get equipment, food, into Sarajevo pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Why did they need to built a tunnel to do that?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but it would do it more easy and more safe to take things into -- to go underground with things than pass the airfield with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Were there more conventional points of entry into Sarajevo that they could have used?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I don't know. I think the best way for all supplies was to come down convoy road into Hrasnica area and then from there get it into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Finally, Major, I want to ask you about the mortars that were placed for a period at Kovaci?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the map I want to look at is D36, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise that map and the markings you were asked to make during your earlier testimony?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: First of all, to correct myself, I think the circle you drew with an S next to it marked the spot where the 17-year-old girl was shot; is that not a proper recollection of mine?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. But the part I'm interested in is the area you've circled marked with the letter M, presumably for mortars.

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You described these four mortars in your statement as 81-millimetre mortars; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you said that as soon as you discovered that the mortars were positioned there that you made sure they were removed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you know when that was?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: The day after we discovered them when we were going up convoy road again, they were removed. So during that evening night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You didn't have them removed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we complained about them, and they -- BiH forces removed them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just that line 7 of paragraph 44 suggests that you had them removed, so I just wanted to make sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we complained about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In terms of trying to place a rough date, was this something that happened early in your time in Hrasnica, or late?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: I had been there for awhile when we saw that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And after you had made the request to have the mortars removed, was there any sign that they were still there, still being used?

utterances.speaker: THORBJORN OVERGARD
utterances.text: No, we passed that backyard several times but never saw things like that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Major, that's all that I have for you. Their Honours may have some questions for you, if you kindly wait there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Thomas. Thank you very much, Mr. Overgard, that concludes your testimony for today and thank you so much for coming and testifying at the Tribunal, you are now excused. You may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Mr. Cannata will lead the next witness. That concludes the business of myself and Ms. McKenna before Your Honours this morning. If I could please be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are excused. Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. With your indulgence, I will switch on to that computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are indulged.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, the Prosecution calls Dr. Youssef Hajir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: It looks like we have a problem getting witnesses into the courtroom today, Your Honour. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May you please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: She will help you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may now be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me reminds Your Honours that Dr. Hajir is a 92 ter witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, good morning.

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you please state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: Dr. Youssef Hajir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Doctor, can you tell the Court what was your profession from May 1992 up to the end of the war, up to the end of 1995? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, I lived in Vrace, and since I was unable to get to work because there were barricades on the road around Sarajevo at Vrace, I was unable to reach my hospital, the clinic, the medical clinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sorry, let me stop you here. Would you mind answering the question I've asked you. Now, the question would be, what was your profession between May 1992 up to the end of the war in 1995? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: I opened the Dobrinja Hospital, I worked there as a director. I was a surgeon and for the most part in this period, I really managed the hospital and performed surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, can I have 65 ter 9396 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY on 17 June, 2008?

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Is that the document in front of you displayed on e-court, the statement you gave and signed on 17 June, 2008?

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, were you asked to review medical documents issued by the Dobrinja Hospital which are listed in your statement?

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: Yes, some medical documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to page 2 of this statement, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you confirm that the documents that are listed at page 2 and 3 of this statement are copies of authentic medical records and certificates issued by the Dobrinja Hospital?

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: I reviewed the documents, and I concluded based on the form of the documents, and the doctors who signed the documents and who were my associates, and also based on documents that I signed, in other words, both based on the signatures, the findings, and the form, they correspond, are consistent with the documents of the Dobrinja Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, do you confirm that this statement, the one that you signed on 17 June, 2008, is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Does the statement accurately reflect what you would say today if asked to speak about the same matters once again?

utterances.speaker: YOUSSEF HAJIR
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I will tender into evidence the statement and some of the medical records associated with that. I have a 65 ter number for each of the documents I would like to tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
